overview: This Senate resolution designates September 2026 as "National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month." It notes that nearly 15,000 children and teens in the United States are diagnosed with cancer each year and about 1,600 die from it, making cancer the leading cause of death from disease among children after infancy. It also notes that survival rates have risen to more than 85 percent, but most survivors develop at least one long-term health problem. The resolution asks governments and nonprofits to hold awareness programs, encourages survivors to get lifelong follow-up care, and pledges to make preventing and curing childhood cancer a public health priority. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say awareness helps families recognize risks, encourages survivors to keep up with follow-up care and builds support for pediatric cancer research.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for childhood cancer research.
